Attorneys That Do Wills in Texas: What You Need to Know

Creating a will is one of the most important legal steps you can take to protect your loved ones and ensure your wishes are honored after your death. Yet many Texans put it off—often because they don’t know where to start or who to trust.

If you're searching for attorneys that do wills in Texas, this guide will walk you through what to expect, how to choose the right lawyer, and why working with a skilled estate planning attorney is far better than using a DIY solution.

At The Lange Firm, based in Sugar Land, Texas, we help individuals and families across the state create wills and estate plans that are tailored, legally sound, and stress-free.

Why You Need an Attorney to Draft Your Will

A last will and testament is a legal document that directs how your assets should be distributed after death. It can also name guardians for minor children, appoint an executor, and help reduce family conflict.

While online templates and DIY kits may seem convenient, they often fail to comply with Texas-specific laws—and a poorly drafted will can lead to costly court battles.

Here’s why working with an attorney is the smart choice:

  • Ensures compliance with Texas law

  • Tailors the will to your family’s needs

  • Avoids probate problems and contests

  • Advises on related documents (like powers of attorney or trusts)

  • Explains how your will fits into a broader estate plan

What Texas Attorneys Who Draft Wills Can Help You With

When you work with a Texas estate planning attorney, they don’t just fill in blanks—they evaluate your entire situation to create a plan that works now and in the future.

Services typically include:

  • Drafting a last will and testament

  • Naming executors and guardians

  • Creating living wills and advance directives

  • Drafting financial and medical powers of attorney

  • Coordinating beneficiary designations

  • Advising on trusts and probate avoidance strategies

An experienced attorney also helps you review and update your will when life changes—such as marriage, divorce, birth of children, or changes in finances.

Who Should Have a Will in Texas?

Every adult should have a will—regardless of wealth, marital status, or age. A will is especially critical if you:

  • Own real estate or valuable personal property

  • Are married or in a long-term relationship

  • Have children or dependents

  • Want to name a legal guardian

  • Want to leave specific gifts or charitable bequests

  • Want to minimize family disputes

Without a valid will, your estate will be distributed according to Texas intestacy laws, which may not reflect your wishes.

What Makes a Will Valid in Texas?

Under Texas Estates Code, a valid will must meet these basic requirements:

  • The testator (person making the will) must be 18 years old, or legally married, or a member of the U.S. armed forces.

  • The testator must be of sound mind at the time of signing.

  • The will must be in writing (handwritten or typed).

  • A typed will must be signed by the testator and two credible witnesses (over age 14), in the testator’s presence.

Texas also recognizes holographic wills (entirely handwritten and signed by the testator), but they are easier to challenge and lack many of the legal protections of a professionally drafted will.

How Much Does It Cost to Have an Attorney Prepare a Will in Texas?

The cost of drafting a will with an attorney in Texas varies based on complexity, location, and whether it’s part of a larger estate plan. In general:

  • A simple will may cost $300–$600.

  • A comprehensive estate plan, including a will, powers of attorney, and possibly a trust, may range from $1,000 to $3,000+.

While the upfront cost is higher than a DIY kit, the long-term savings in court fees, family disputes, and tax consequences are often substantial.

At The Lange Firm, we offer transparent, flat-fee pricing for many estate planning packages—and ensure your documents are customized to your needs.

Common Mistakes Made Without an Attorney

If you create a will without legal guidance, you may run into serious problems, such as:

  • Failing to comply with Texas signature and witness laws

  • Naming an ineligible executor

  • Not addressing out-of-state property

  • Leaving out contingent beneficiaries

  • Creating vague language that leads to family disputes

  • Overlooking digital assets, business interests, or debts

An experienced attorney helps you avoid these errors and ensures your will holds up in court.

The Role of a Will in a Larger Estate Plan

While a will is essential, it’s only part of a full estate plan. Many Texans also need:

  • A revocable living trust to avoid probate

  • Healthcare documents like a medical power of attorney

  • A financial power of attorney for incapacity

  • A living will to express end-of-life wishes

  • Beneficiary coordination across accounts and policies

When you work with a law firm like The Lange Firm, you receive a comprehensive, cohesive plan—not just a will in isolation.

Choosing the Right Attorney for Wills in Texas

When looking for a will attorney, consider the following:

✅ Texas-Specific Experience

Choose someone who understands the Texas Estates Code, probate procedures, and local court systems.

✅ Focus on Estate Planning

Work with a lawyer who focuses primarily on estate planning and probate law, not someone who dabbles in multiple unrelated areas.

✅ Clear Pricing

Ask about flat fees or packages so you know what to expect.

✅ Client-Focused Approach

You want a lawyer who takes the time to understand your family dynamics, values, and goals.

Why Choose The Lange Firm?

At The Lange Firm in Sugar Land, Texas, we help clients throughout the state create wills that reflect their wishes and protect their families. Here’s why Texans trust us with their estate plans:

  • Focused estate planning practice

  • Flat-fee pricing and no hidden costs

  • Personalized service tailored to your goals

  • Knowledge of Texas probate and property laws

  • Guidance beyond just wills—full estate strategies

Whether you’re creating a will for the first time or updating an old one, we’ll make the process simple, professional, and effective.

Final Thoughts

If you're searching for attorneys that do wills in Texas, you’re already taking a critical step in protecting your legacy. But don’t settle for a generic template or cookie-cutter advice. Work with an attorney who understands your unique situation and the laws that apply in Texas.

At The Lange Firm, we’re here to help you craft a legally sound will and an estate plan that gives your family peace of mind—now and for generations to come. For addition probate information visit the probate home page.
